target_customer: Public transit agencies (small and mid-size) that pay for fare payment and mobile ticketing, with riders as end users
problem: Transit agencies lacked affordable modern fare payment, and riders had to use cash or paper tickets. Founders found fare payment to be a major pain point after interviewing hundreds of agency experts.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments platform sold to transit agencies, with fees on fare transactions
product_category: Transit fare payment and mobile ticketing platform

founders.name: Morgan Kikuchi-Conbere
founders.background_notes: YC page says he never learned to drive and works with cities on transport infrastructure. The company founding story page says the founders brought software experience from Google and Apple but does not say who worked where.

founders.name: Zachary Browne
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has never owned a car.

founders.name: Ekate Kuznetsova
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. The founding story page says she joined to help build the first mobile ticketing app.

founders.name: Sam Daly
founders.background_notes: Named a founder on the company founding story page, which says he approached Zack and Morgan in 2015. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Masabi
competitors.what: Mobile ticketing platform (JustRide) behind many agency apps
competitors.traction_then: JustRide app was a finalist for Transit App of the Year in 2016

competitors.name: Moovit
competitors.what: Trip planning app with a transit tools business
competitors.traction_then: Named as a 2016 finalist alongside Masabi in the same source; later enabled ticket purchase for small agencies

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile ticketing needed secure visual and barcode tickets, payments and agency integrations, standard engineering with some hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Agency contracts and integrations with farebox and trip planners create switching costs, but ticketing apps from Masabi and others were already sold to agencies.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were established but none absorbed the small agency niche; the company stayed independent and the YC page lists it active.

market_need_then: In 2016 a Boston Fed review listed several transit mobile ticketing apps, and a Masabi release cited research that most US agencies planned mobile ticketing. Many small agencies still had cash and paper fares.

branding.domain_note: Uses tokentransit.com; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: No source covers press on the brand itself; agencies often deploy white label apps under the agency name, so the brand is secondary.

outcome_analysis: Token Transit signed its first agency contract in Reno, grew to over 200 agencies in the US and Canada and links into Transit, Moovit and Google Maps, which gives it distribution that rivals lacked. It raised only about 4 million dollars per aggregators and stayed small, with a team of about 12 on the YC page. Competitors Passport and Masabi were large, and Passport shut its ticketing business in 2022, which moved riders onto Token Transit in Detroit.
notes: Funding: Dynamo Ventures portfolio page says a 4.1M seed; CB Insights and Caplight label a 4.12M Series A in Oct or Nov 2019 with 4.49M total over four rounds. Label conflict, so stage is other. Earlier seed amounts not found. No outcome news of acquisition or shutdown found. Name origin and logo not found in any source.
